messages.author: bccf789db78f8994
messages.subject: Effect Plots for RQTL2
parts:
In the RQTL package we were able to pull out an effect plot for a specific marker (using find.marker and effectplot)

I am interested in doing this in the RQTL2 package with find_marker but, I do not see the equivalent to effectplot for the new package. Is there an equivalent?

If there is no direct equivalent, is there a way to modify the qtl effects plot described in the RQTL2 user manual to only display a region of a chromosome, rather than the entire chromosome?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: Effect Plots for RQTL2
parts:
I recently added a function plot_pxg() in the qtl2plot package, which hopefully does what you want.
I've not yet added it to the R/qtl2 user guide. 

karl

messages.subject: Re: Effect Plots for RQTL2
parts:
Hi Karl,

What exactly are we looking at in the plot_pxg() output? I am using this to analyze one of the significant loci we found using the DO population so I see that the founder strains are represented here. The output graph I see only has 7 of the founder strains. What does it mean that the 8th is not present? Also, where are all the points for each founder strain coming? I only fed in one genotype per founder strain in the founder_geno input matrix.

Thanks!

Avni

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect Plots for RQTL2
parts:
The input 'geno' should be a vector of genotypes. The plot will show the phenotypes split up by genotype group.

Try table(geno) where geno is the object you're passing to plot_pxg(). Yes; as you say, perhaps one of the genotypes is not present at this locus.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] Effect Plots for RQTL2
parts:
>
> Ok, I think I need to take a step back... I don't think I understand what maxmarg() does.
>
> 1) Is the output of maxmarg() telling me what founder genotype each of my samples looks like at the given locus?
For each individual, it returns the genotype with highest probability, provided it is > minprob (which has a default value of 0.95).

> 2) Is the fact that one of the founder strains isn't present on the plot_pxg() graph indicative that none of the samples look like this founder strain at the given locus?
>
